info.title: NVIDIA Attribution Service
info.summary: Service for producing failure attribution/workload information from metrics & logs
info.description:
NVIDIA Attribution Service helps interpret workload information (primarily failures).

It produces 'attributions', typically node-based, based on 'observations'.

The model is that POSTing to the '/attributor' endpoint with some workload information plus agent metadata creates a handle that is returned to the user.

The handle can then be used as follows:

* POSTing 'observations' to '/attributor/{handle}/observation' feeds logs/metrics/etc to the service and associates them with the handle. Each such POST will produce an 'observation_id' that can be used to track the ingestion of the observation.

* GETing '/attributor/{handle}/attribution' will produce an attribution that tries to explain how the workload failed (if it did) and explains how the service reached that conclusion.

* DELETEing '/attributor/{handle}' will clean up that handle.

It is possible to interleave observation-posting and attribution-getting; the more observations that have been ingested, the better the quality of the attribution, generally speaking.

post.description: Create a new attribution attributor based on provided metadata and return an id with which to identify it. Providing identical metadata to an existing attributor is an error.

Pass observation to specified attributor and return an id that identifies it. It is an error to provide a duplicate observation. When the id is returned, the observation has been successfully ingested.

get.description: Perform attribution on specified attributor based on all previous observation ingested on this attributor.

delete.description: Destroy attribution attributor indicated by id. It is an error if the id is not present in the service.

EventStorageOverflowError.title: EventStorageOverflowError
EventStorageOverflowError.description:
Error for when an attributor's event storage exceeds its memory budget.

Raised instead of a generic 500 when ATTRIBUTOR_ALLOW_DISK_SPILL=false
(the default for containerized deployments with no writable disk) and an
attributor's DuckDB connection exceeds ATTRIBUTOR_DUCKDB_MEMORY_LIMIT.
Isolated to the one attributor/request that triggered it.

Format.title: Format
Format.description:
Specifies the types of formats the 'lines' in an observation can be in.

Not all sources can be specified in each format; see above for clarification.

Furthermore, some sources expect slightly different fields in formats.

In particular, the `applog` source expects the entry found in the given format to have a rank-like prefix; for them, the host-specifier field, if present in a format, is optional. `entry_timeseries` is the exception: it parses the prefix only out of an entry that declares no `resources`, and a body timestamp only when `ts` is null (see below).

For `syslog` and `health_check`, the rank-like prefix is not expected, and `host-specifier` fields are mandatory.

Rank-like prefixes are match the following regex: "^\[rank\s*:?\s*(?P<rank>\d+)\]" or have an integer followed by a colon at the start of the line.

Examples:

    [rank3] Message
     3: another message
    [rank :10] a third message


- `string_list`:

    Raw text

    Lines of text separated by newlines. No hosts associations.

- `raw_log`:

    Raw text

    entries separated by newlines. Rank-like prefix expected for applog.

- `raw_loki_streams`:

    JSON-based

    Top-Level Structure:
    - An array of objects, each with:
      - `stream`: If host-spcifier needed, *Required*. If present, must contain the `node_name` field (string); which is the host-specifier. All other fields in stream are permitted but ignored.
      - `values`: *Required*. An array of entries.

    Details:
    - `stream` Object. *Required* if host-specifier:
      - Required Field:
        - `node_name` (string): Identifies the node that generated the logs. Host specifier.
        - Other fields: Any other fields within stream are permitted but ignored.
    - `values` Array:
      - Each entry is a 2-element array:
        - Timestamp (string): Unix timestamp; unit scale dictated by Source (see above).
        - Entry (string): the main content. Should have rank-line prefix for applog.
    - Other fields:
      - Any other fields at any level are permitted but ignored.

    Example (`syslog` source):
    ```json
    [
      {
        "stream": {
          "node_name": "host-a1b2c3d4"
        },
        "values": [
          [
            "1744734437830498000",
            "Apr 24 12:04:06 host-a1b2c3d4 kernel: message repeated 8 times: [ NVRM: subdeviceCtrlCmdBusGetNvlinkStatus_IMPL: Failed to collect nvlink status info!]"
          ]
        ]
      }
    ]
    ```

- `loki_dict_list`:

    JSON-based.

    Top-Level Structure:
    -  An array of objects, each with:
        - `values`: Required. An array of entries.

    Details:
    - `values` Array:
      Each entry is a 2-element array:
      - Timestamp (string): Unix timestamp; unit scale dictated by Source (see above).
      - Content (string): A JSON-encoded object with at least the following fields:
        - `body` (string): entry (required; rank-like prefix expected for APPLOG.)
        - `hostname` (string): The source hostname (required if host-specified needed.)
    - Other fields:
      - The `stream` object is optional and, if present, is ignored.
      - Any other fields in the log message JSON are permitted but ignored.

    Example (`syslog` source)
    ```json
    [
      {
        "values": [
          [
            "1744734421212766000",
            "{\"body\":\"Some log message\",\"hostname\":\"server-01\"}"
          ]
        ]
      }
    ]
    ```

- `csv_metric_response`:

  Not implemented presently.

- `prometheus_metrics`:

  JSON-based.

  Top-Level Structure:
  - An array of objects, each representing a metric data point.

  Details:
  - Each object must contain:
    - `timestamp` (int): Unix timestamp in seconds
    - `value` (Union[int, float, string]): Metric value (initially as string, converted later)
    - `metric` (string): Metric name (e.g., "node_infiniband_link_downed_total")
    - `labels` (dict): Prometheus labels including node and device information
    - `node` (string): Node identifier (required, extracted from net_host_name label)
    - `component` (string, optional): Component/device identifier (e.g., "mlx5_0", "mlx5_1")
    - `cluster` (string, optional): Cluster identifier (e.g., "cluster-e5f6g7h8", extracted from s_cluster label)

  Example:
  ```json
  [
    {
      "timestamp": 1753898040,
      "value": "1",
      "metric": "node_infiniband_link_downed_total",
      "labels": {
        "net_host_name": "host-i9j0k1l2",
        "s_cluster": "cluster-e5f6g7h8",
        "device": "mlx5_0",
        "instance": "host-i9j0k1l2:9100"
      },
      "node": "host-i9j0k1l2",
      "component": "mlx5_0",
      "cluster": "cluster-e5f6g7h8"
    }
  ]
  ```

- `entry_timeseries`:

  JSON-based.

  Top-Level Structure:
  - An array of entry objects.

  Details:
  - Each entry object contains:
    - `body` (string): *Required*. Matched verbatim. Parsed only as the per-source fallback
      described below.
    - `ts` (int or null): Unix timestamp in **nanoseconds**, or null/absent when the producer
      has no timestamp for this entry. It means "this entry occurred no later than this time".
      May be parsed from body and/or dropped if none given for some sources.
    - `resources` (optional): What this entry is about. Either the exact string `"AllJobResources"`
      or an array naming exactly one `{"kind": "node", "hostname": ...}`, optionally alongside
      `{"kind": "replica", "name": ...}` objects, which are recorded but not attributed on. An array
      naming several nodes, or a hostname outside the job, is invalid and handled like an entry naming
      no node. Node may be parsed from body and/or dropped if none given for some sources.
  - Any other key in an entry is rejected.

  Unlike every other format, entries here are only time-filtered by the observation context's
  `time_interval`. That interval is the producer's declared intent: a null bound means unbounded on
  that side, so an interval of two nulls disables time filtering for the observation entirely.

  Key Source Behavior:

  The sources listed below read an entry the same way unless noted; a source not listed requires
  nothing and parses nothing out of the body.
  - `ts` is required: an entry without it is dropped.
  - A declared node is used as-is, so a host specifier in IP form must be resolved by the producer. If
    no node is declared, the node is parsed out of the body instead, keeping any declared replicas. An
    entry that still names no node is dropped.
  - `body` is the line as received. The library never parses its shape beyond the fallbacks
    noted below; what a body must look like is whatever the source's rules match.

  Deviations:
  - `applog`:
    - `ts` can be null, in which case the body is parsed for a timestamp. Year-less formats resolve it
      against the workload's `job_end_time`.
    - The body node is parsed from the rank-like or node-name text prefix. An entry that still names no node,
      or names an invalid one, is recorded against every job resource instead of dropped. An explicit
      `"AllJobResources"` skips the prefix parse altogether.
  - `syslog` & `health_check`: the node is parsed from the hostname field of the body.
  - `ufmlog`:
    - `ts` can be null, in which case the entry is kept and treated as untimed.
    - The body node is parsed from either the link form `(Computer:<node> (<guid>))` or the node
      form `(<node>) node is Down`.
  - `node_metrics` and `nvlink_metrics`:
    - `ts` can be null, in which case the entry is kept and treated as untimed.
    - `resources` must name the node; the body is never parsed for one.
  - `csp_event`:
    - `ts` must be set; the body is never parsed for one. An entry without it is dropped.
    - `resources` must name the node; the body is never parsed for one.
    - There is no received line: producers render the body as
      `csp_event: category=<category>, reason=<reason>, status=<status>`, optionally followed by
      `, source_event=<compact JSON, sorted keys>` carrying the provider payload.

  Example:
  ```json
  [
    {
      "ts": 1744734437830498000,
      "resources": [{"kind": "node", "hostname": "host-a1b2c3d4"}],
      "body": "some log message"
    },
    {
      "body": "an untimed entry; kept or dropped per the source rules above"
    }
  ]
  ```

time_interval.description: The collection window: the interval the entries were deliberately gathered over. The service filters entries by it; an entry whose timestamp falls outside the window is discarded and never reaches a rule. Specifying `None` for either bound is allowed, and treats the observation as unbounded on that side. `start` must not be later than `end`.

Scheduler.title: Scheduler
Scheduler.description:
Recognized values for `JobInfo.scheduler`.

Unlike `JobInfo.type`, which is a free-form legacy wire token, every
`JobInfo.scheduler` value is one of these members. `UNKNOWN` means "no
recognized scheduler identity": callers must not use it to build a
rendered ID and should fall back to generic wording. Existing Slurm
symptom strings are unchanged.

Source.title: Source
Source.description:
The classes of observations that can be ingested.

`job_keywords` takes the `string_list` format; every other implemented source takes `entry_timeseries`.
See `Format` for how each source reads its entries.

- `slurm_info`

    Automatically attached to JobInfo objects; not supported for other Observations. No relevant Format.

- `job_keywords`

    Keywords extracted from preprocessing some logs.

- `applog`

    Application's stdout/stderr.

- `syslog`

    Data from dmesg/syslog.

- `health_check`

    Data from health checks.

- `ufmlog`

    Fabric manager events.

- `node_metrics`

   Prometheus metrics data for node attribution.

- `nvlink_metrics`

   Prometheus metrics data for nvlink attribution.

- `ib_metrics`

   Not implemented.

- `eth_metrics`

   Not implemented.

- `network_syslog`

   Not implemented.

- `csp_event`

   CSP event events indicating infrastructure-level host failures,
   repairs, or maintenance actions reported by the cloud service provider.

catalog_id.title: Catalog Id
catalog_id.description: Documentation slug identifying the failure-catalog entry this symptom maps to. A reference into that catalog, not a guaranteed-unique key per symptom.

SourcedSymptom.title: SourcedSymptom
SourcedSymptom.description: A symptom paired with the specific source that surfaced it.

SymptomStatus.title: SymptomStatus
SymptomStatus.description: Whether a source still drives attribution, or was demoted to supporting evidence.

TerminalState.title: TerminalState
TerminalState.description:
What happened to the job. Always present; every outcome maps to at
least one of these (possibly more than one, when NVIDIA Attribution can't
narrow it down further -- see "Incomplete Info" in `_OUTCOME_TABLE`).

TimeInterval.title: TimeInterval
TimeInterval.description:
The window an observation declares it covers.

Both keys are required, so a payload that omits one is a validation error rather than unbounded.
A null bound means unbounded on that side, and only the `entry_timeseries` format accepts one.

TimeIntervalV2.title: TimeIntervalV2
TimeIntervalV2.description: The window the entries were collected over. A null bound is unbounded on that side.

UncertaintyType.title: UncertaintyType
UncertaintyType.description:
NVIDIA Attribution's qualitative classification of the source of uncertainty.

ALEATORIC describes ambiguity in the available job evidence, including
insufficient data ("Incomplete Info"). It does not assert that the job
behaved randomly or that better observations could never resolve it.
EPISTEMIC describes limitations of NVIDIA Attribution itself, such as missing rules or
bugs ("Fail Undetermined"). These are the operational definitions from
the compound-outcome RFC, not a general statistical uncertainty model.

Neither value measures likelihood, confidence, severity, or an error rate.
None means no uncertainty source is reported, not guaranteed correctness.
The source is supplied explicitly, not inferred from the possibility count.

UnknownAttributorIdError.title: UnknownAttributorIdError
UnknownAttributorIdError.description: Error for when an attributor id is not known to the attribution service.

UnknownObservationFormatError.title: UnknownObservationFormatError
UnknownObservationFormatError.description: Error for when we receive an unknown observation format

ValidationErrorResponse.title: ValidationErrorResponse
ValidationErrorResponse.description: Published schema for the validation envelope returned by the application handlers.

terminal_states.title: Terminal States
terminal_states.description: Plausible terminal states in NVIDIA Attribution's assessment. Values are alternatives, with no ranking or probabilities; omitted states are ruled out by that assessment. A singleton does not guarantee correctness, and the number of values is not a confidence score.

failure_domains.title: Failure Domains
failure_domains.description: Plausible failure domains, conditional on Fail. Values express alternatives, not simultaneous causes or equal probabilities. Empty means failure is absent or its domain is unspecified; consult terminal_states to distinguish these cases.

cancellation_actors.title: Cancellation Actors
cancellation_actors.description: Plausible initiators, conditional on Cancelled. Values express alternatives without ranking or probabilities. Empty means cancellation is absent or its actor is unspecified; consult terminal_states to distinguish these cases.

uncertainty_type.description: Qualitative source of uncertainty using NVIDIA Attribution's operational definitions: Aleatoric means ambiguous or insufficient job evidence; Epistemic means limitations of NVIDIA Attribution, such as rule gaps or bugs. This is not a probability, confidence score, or error rate. Null means no source is reported, not guaranteed correctness. The source is not inferred from set size.

decision_graph.description: Runtime Decision DAG: the graph when requested and available, null when requested but unavailable, absent when not requested.

Verdict.title: Verdict
Verdict.description: Top-level attribution outcome: raw lib outcome, free-form detail, and the driving root-cause symptom if any.
